raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Extend the routed CPU MoE dispatch approach from [#50949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50949) to INT8 W8A8: select brgemm from each expert tile's actual row count instead of the call-wide average. Use brgemm for four-row tiles and share the existing tinygemm arithmetic between BF16 and FP16.

On a 32-core Qwen3 W8A8 serving comparison, the change improves the geometric mean of output throughput across nine concurrency levels by 1.41%, with 5.76% at concurrency 32 and 4.42% at concurrency 64. Peak-concurrency throughput remains at parity. The concurrency-32 baseline varies between repeats; both runs are shown below.

As #50949 describes the approach:
> Select BRGEMM from each expert block's actual `M` and `N`.

Open-PR searches for CPU INT8 MoE and routed GEMM dispatch found no duplicate. #50949 covers FP8/MXFP4; this change covers the separate INT8 W8A8 implementation.

## Claims

- Concentrated routing can use brgemm even when the average tokens per expert would select tinygemm.
- Both routed INT8 GEMM stages select their kernel per tile and release brgemm state when used by the parallel callback.
- BF16 and FP16 support small expert tiles through the same VNNI arithmetic, with conversion directly to the requested intermediate dtype.

## Validation

Reviewed head: `cedc8f26c0`; branch base: `9f3d70e081`.

```bash
# Focused checks: 68 passed during PR readiness review
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py \
  -k 'int8_w8a8 or small_expert_blocks' \
  tests/kernels/test_awq_int4_to_int8.py::TestInt4ScaledMmCpu -q

pre-commit run --files csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/gemm.h \
  csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/moe_int8.cpp \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py
git diff --check 9f3d70e081 HEAD
```

All applicable hooks passed. The BF16/FP16 test covers expert occupancies `(3, 4, 5, 33)`, including mixed dispatch and a block tail, and runs in CPU kernel CI. Commands omit host-specific affinity settings.

### Serving comparison

Following #50949's Sonnet 256/256 concurrency sweep, compare the same base and candidate with `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w8a8` (revision `b2b37fb1c4cd5a5769b841ef1f672627b8304d8e`), BF16, TP=1, DP=1, and 32 physical compute cores.

| Concurrency | Base output tok/s (runs 1 / 2) | Candidate output tok/s (runs 1 / 2) | Mean throughput change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 35.19 / 35.21 | 35.14 / 35.07 | -0.26% |
| 2 | 53.20 / 53.16 | 53.07 / 53.18 | -0.09% |
| 4 | 82.35 / 82.31 | 82.57 / 82.45 | +0.22% |
| 8 | 130.33 / 130.31 | 131.64 / 131.43 | +0.93% |
| 16 | 192.93 / 191.13 | 195.61 / 195.89 | +1.94% |
| 32 | 294.42 / 279.66 | 303.41 / 303.74 | +5.76% |
| 64 | 437.61 / 435.76 | 456.60 / 455.33 | +4.42% |
| 128 | 654.13 / 654.97 | 652.40 / 655.86 | -0.06% |
| 256 | 872.06 / 871.38 | 872.51 / 871.71 | +0.04% |

## Details

The previous selector uses `max(1, M * topk / E)` for the whole call. That average hides concentrated routing and expert-block tails. Both stages now use actual tile dimensions, skip empty tiles, and track brgemm use within each parallel callback.

The routed INT8 two-argument selector uses `M > 3` for full-width tiles. The existing one-argument selector continues to serve INT8 linear, INT4, and shared-expert callers. FP8/MXFP4 thresholds are unchanged.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and this description.

files.patch:
@@ -1114,6 +1114,40 @@ def test_int8_w8a8_cpu_fused_moe(M, N, K, E, topk, seed, is_vnni, inplace):
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+def test_int8_w8a8_cpu_fused_moe_small_expert_blocks(dtype):
+    """Test INT8 dispatch at exact and multi-block expert boundaries."""
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    block_sizes = (3, 4, 5, 33)
+    N, K, E = 128, 128, len(block_sizes)
+    M = sum(block_sizes)
+
+    a = torch.randn(M, K, dtype=dtype) / (0.5 * K**0.5)
+    w1_q, w2_q, w1_s, w2_s = _make_int8_moe_weights(E, N, K)
+    topk_weight, topk_ids = _deterministic_expert_routes(block_sizes)
+
+    ref_out = _ref_int8_moe(a, w1_q, w2_q, w1_s, w2_s, topk_weight, topk_ids)
+    pw1, pw2 = _prepack_experts(w1_q), _prepack_experts(w2_q)
+    out = torch.empty_like(a)
+    ops.fused_experts_cpu(
+        out,
+        a,
+        pw1,
+        pw2,
+        topk_weight,
+        topk_ids,
+        ops.CPUQuantMethod.INT8_W8A8,
+        w1_s,
+        w2_s,
+        None,
+        None,
+        None,
+        is_vnni=True,
+    )
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ref_out, out, atol=2e-1, rtol=2e-1)
+
+
 # ===========================================================================
 # FP8 W8A8 MoE
 # ===========================================================================
